title: Store Initialization and Hydration
description: Learn how to initialize the Redux store with persisted state, hydrate from localStorage, and handle versioning safely.

data.text: By default, Redux state **disappears on page reload**. Hydration lets you rebuild the store from saved data so users return to exactly where they left off — open tabs, theme choice, drafts, and more.

data.title: What is hydration?
data.text: **Hydration** = loading persisted state into a fresh store before the app mounts. **Persistence** = saving state changes back to storage as the user works.
The classic pattern is: load saved state, pass it to `configureStore` as `preloadedState`, and then subscribe to the store to keep saving changes.

data.title: Manual hydration

data.caption: Hydration loads saved state once; persistence saves it on every change.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Browser
  participant Storage as localStorage
  participant Store as Redux Store
  participant App as React App

  Browser->>Storage: getItem('app:state:v1')
  Storage-->>Browser: serialized JSON
  Browser->>Store: configureStore({ preloadedState })
  Store-->>App: <Provider store={...}>
  App->>App: Render with hydrated state
  App->>Store: dispatch(action)
  Store->>Storage: setItem('app:state:v1', newJSON)

data.title: Storage options compared
rows: User preferences, drafts, non-sensitive UI state

cards.title: localStorage
cards.description: Simple key/value store that survives reloads and tab closures.
cons: Accessible to any script on the page (XSS risk)

cards.title: sessionStorage
cards.description: Same as localStorage but scoped to the current browser tab.
cons: Lost on tab close — bad for preferences

cards.title: Cookies
cards.description: Sent on every HTTP request. Marked httpOnly + secure when set by the server.
pros: Can be flagged httpOnly to block JS access

data.text: When you change your state shape, old saved data can break your app. Use a **version key** in the persisted blob and run migrations when the versions don't match.

data.title: Versioned persistence

data.text: Saving on every dispatch is expensive — especially for large state trees. **Debounce** the save so it only fires after the user pauses.

data.title: Debounced persistence
data.content: Save state every 500 ms instead of every action

terms.definition: Initial state passed to `configureStore`. Used to inject hydrated data.
The act of loading persisted state into a fresh Redux store before mounting React.
Code that transforms old persisted state into the shape your current reducers expect.
Delaying repeated writes so they only happen after activity stops.

data.title: Security
data.text: Never persist sensitive data — passwords, refresh tokens, PII — in Redux or localStorage. Use httpOnly cookies or a server session instead.

data.title: Implement versioned hydration
data.description:
Write a `createPersistedStore(rootReducer, options)` helper that:
1. Reads state from localStorage under a key you pass in.
2. Checks a `version` field; if it doesn't match `options.version`, return `undefined`.
3. Subscribes to the store and saves the state with the version field.
4. Wraps the save in a `try/catch` so quota errors don't crash the app.
steps: `JSON.stringify` will throw if your state contains a circular reference.
Throttle the subscribe handler if the reducer fires often.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `preloadedState` to hydrate from saved data
Persist with `store.subscribe`, debounced to avoid wasted writes
Version your persisted state and migrate or discard when shapes change
Pick storage based on size, lifetime, and sensitivity
Never persist auth tokens or PII in client storage
data.takeaway: Hydration preserves state across sessions and keeps users in flow.
